newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn deputy urges CDU learn from Britain, France.
newsitem.headline: Bonn deputy urges CDU learn from Britain, France.

text.p: An outspoken critic of German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in his own Christian Democrats (CDU) has warned his party to take note of the recent election defeats of British and French conservatives, a newspaper said on Wednesday.
Heiner Geissler, deputy parliamentary leader of the CDU, told the Berliner Morgenpost daily the British and French elections should be taken as a warning signal for Kohl's party.
"The decisions currently under consideration are being met as if we don't care about the marginalisation of millions of people," the paper quoted Geissler as saying.
Geissler, who has often spoken out about government policies he disagrees with, said Bonn could not expect to stop gaping budget holes with further social spending cuts.

He said the government should instead raise indirect taxes while lowering direct taxation and he also supported Bonn's controversial plan to raise cash by revaluing Bundesbank currency and gold reserves.
"We could even sell it (the gold)," Geissler said, adding that whether the Bundesbank held 2,900 tonnes of gold or five ounces had nothing to do with the deutschemark's stability.

But he said Bonn's attempt to push through the plan without the Bundesbank's agreement was dangerous for the financial and economic reputation of the CDU and sister party the Christian Social Union (CSU).
Kohl's government on Tuesday retreated from the controversial plan to revalue central bank reserves.

Geissler said Europe's single currency should be introduced on time in 1999 and that this timetable should take precedence of the three percent government deficit to gross domestic product target Germany is struggling to fulfill.
"A delay would be a real catastrophe. The euro would then be finally dead in my opinion, he said.
He criticised Finance Minister Theo Waigel for "dogmatically" asserting that the deficit criteria had to be rigidly interpreted.
